title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 8

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the PLC table lesson begin?
tasks.audioText: The control systems instructor will review a sample PLC input-output table on Wednesday at nine forty-five. Students should bring the controller reference sheet and meet in the automation room. The class will identify the difference between a physical input, a programme variable and an output reference. The exercise will use a printed table only.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which safety-symbol reference material should students bring?

Students should bring the controller reference sheet and meet in the automation room. The class will identify the difference between a physical input, a programme variable and an output reference. tasks.prompt: A PLC input-output table links field devices with the controller's documented addresses. The table may include a device description, signal type and address. A programme variable can use a separate symbolic name to make the logic easier to understand. The relationship between physical addresses and programme names should be documented clearly so that maintenance staff can interpret the system information. Reading 1. What information may appear in a PLC input-output table?
options: Device description, signal type and address
They make programme logic easier to understand

tasks.prompt: The physical address ___ in the input-output table.
Choose TWO fields that may appear in a PLC input-output table.
A name used in a programme to represent a value or item is a ___.
A symbolic variable is not linked clearly to a physical address. What should you ask?
options: I will create a link from memory.
Could we check the address mapping in the approved PLC documentation?

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of PLC input and output records in a logical order.
Write 80–100 words explaining why PLC input-output records should link device descriptions, signal addresses and symbolic names.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: device descriptions, signal addresses and symbolic names are all addressed (0–2); the response explains how linking them supports traceability and consistent interpretation of PLC inputs/outputs (0–2); the explanation is logically organised with understandable grammar (0–2); PLC/I-O documentation vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
